pages.text: Pipi called a station, and the train stopped by a river. An unfamiliar goat stood on the platform with no luggage. Dad got down to check the wheels, and Bami hid behind him.
As a conductor in training, Bami should greet passengers. But 'Hello' stuck in their throat. Their heart thumped. "I want to greet him... What do I say to someone new?"
The goat boarded the dining car alone and sat in a corner by the door. Through the window, Bami saw his trembling ears. Wanting to greet him but unable to, Bami nearly cried.
Dad knelt beside Bami. "See his ears trembling? It's his first ride on our train. He's nervous, too." Bami's eyes widened. "Grown-ups get nervous?"
Dad whispered, "Just one greeting. Look at him, bow your head, and say hello! He'll bow back." Dad showed a bow. Bami practiced inside their beak. "Hello..."
Bami took a big breath and climbed the dining-car steps one by one. Dad nodded from the doorway. The goat looked up from his corner.
Bami spread their wings and bowed. "Hello! Welcome to Bami's train!" Their voice trembled a little, but came out bravely. They had done it! Just say hello!
The goat smiled and bowed back. "Hello! It's my first train ride." Bami tapped the window seat. "Best place! You can see the whole river." His ears stopped trembling.
Now Bami knew the greeting steps. "One, look in their eyes! Two, bow! Three, say hello!" At the next station, Bami greeted the next passenger first.
That evening, Dad hugged Bami. "What a wonderful greeting, Conductor!" Even with nerves, one hello could make a new acquaintance a friend. Just say hello!
